title: Marine Non-Reefer Cargo - Owner-Approved Methodology Profile

evidence_terms_any: mode of conveyance by sea freight

section_order: INTEREST INSURED & RELEVANT CONDITIONS OF INSURANCE POLICY
CONTAINER, PACKING, HANDLING OR TESTING REVIEW when material
CLAIM PRESENTED ON THE POLICY & ADJUSTMENT
style_notes: Use this profile only for a current containerized or packaged non-refrigerated sea-cargo claim that satisfies the applicability scope; never infer a current claim fact from this profile or from a historical report.

Open with a concise appointment and scope statement identifying the instructing party, policyholder, Assured or claimant, insured interest, reported sea-transit loss, investigation purpose, attendance basis, and whether the report is preliminary or final from current evidence.

Resolve the applicant, insurer, policyholder, Assured, seller, shipper, consignee, buyer, notify party, freight forwarder, contracting and actual carrier, carrier agent, vessel interest, terminal, stevedore, inland haulier, warehouse, customs interest, surveyor, supplier, repairer, salvage buyer and destruction contractor before discussing custody, interest, liability or recovery.

Keep every original, sea waybill or draft bill of lading, booking, carrier tracking record, delivery order, proof of delivery, equipment interchange receipt, gate record, customs record, transport slip and empty-return record separate. Shipper's load, stow and count wording and apparent-good-order receipt do not establish concealed quantity, internal condition or adequate packing.

Reconstruct the supported route chronologically from origin warehouse, stuffing and carrier acceptance through mother vessel, every discharge, transshipment, feeder vessel, port arrival, discharge, gate-out, inland delivery, door opening, unloading and empty return. Distinguish scheduled routing from actual tracking events and preserve voyage-number or date conflicts.

Treat every container separately by number, type, size, seal, packages, weight, cargo allocation and outcome. Distinguish standard dry, high-cube, open-top, flat-rack and other special equipment and record accepted over-height, out-of-gauge or deck-carriage conditions only when current evidence supports them.

Build a condition and custody chain from pre-loading photographs, clean or claused transport acceptance, stuffing and lashing evidence, carrier and terminal records, equipment interchange receipts, delivery reservations, door-opening evidence, joint survey, segregation, repair, salvage and destruction. A tracking event proves movement, not cargo condition.

For packing, stowage and lashing, identify who performed and controlled each operation; the cargo's fragility, dimensions and weight; crates, cartons, pallets, wrapping, cushioning, void filling, blocking, bracing, straps and load distribution; container clearances; handling marks; and the ordinary rigours of the supported voyage. Missing photographs prove neither compliance nor breach.

For impact, crushing or breakage, test pre-shipment condition, damage geometry, distribution within the container, affected versus intact packages, container dents or marks, special height or position, spreader or crane clearance, shifting, contact points, door-side exposure, transshipment handling and unloading. Do not state hard impact or rough handling merely because glass or fragile cargo arrived broken.

For open-top or out-of-gauge cargo, test the declared and accepted dimensions, over-height allowance, tarpaulin or cover, lifting plan, spreader clearance, terminal and vessel handling sequence, securing method, visible crush pattern and whether the alleged mechanism is physically consistent with the location of damage.

For wetting, rust, oxidation or contamination, inspect the container roof, sides, doors, floor, vents and seals; distinguish puncture, structural defect, seawater ingress, freshwater or rain, condensation or sweat, pre-shipment moisture, cleaning residues and post-delivery exposure; correlate the damage pattern and timing with the supported custody chain.

Treat silver-nitrate, chloride, salinity, moisture or other field tests as screening evidence unless the current record establishes sample location and identity, collection method, custody, equipment, reagents, calibration or controls, result, comparator and limitations. Chloride detection can support saline contamination but does not by itself prove the entry route, timing or responsible custodian.

For shortage or non-delivery, reconcile manifested, invoiced, packed, stuffed, carried, discharged, delivered, counted, damaged, missing and claimed quantities; identify who counted or witnessed each stage; review seal and access history, shortlanding certificates, tally and carrier attendance; and preserve origin short-loading, counting error, theft, customs intervention and delivery error as alternatives where viable.

Record notification, appointment, first contact, carrier notice, reserve letter, survey invitation, attendance or abstention, joint survey, signed statement of facts, segregation, mitigation, repair decision, salvage and destruction chronologically. Distinguish a carrier's abstention from an admission of liability.

For delayed or concealed damage, establish when damage was reasonably discoverable, the delivery annotations, notice terms, actual notice date, explanations for delay, evidence preservation and resulting prejudice. Do not declare recovery waived or apply a recovery deduction without the current contract, applicable law, limitation evidence and a reasoned quantification.

Reconcile the damage extent at the smallest supported level: container, package, carton, piece, panel, machine, component, batch, weight and condition category. Keep initial allegations, consignee lists, survey counts, signed statements, invoices, photographs and final segregation results distinct where they conflict.

A total-loss conclusion requires evidence that the identified affected property is physically or functionally unfit, cannot be economically repaired or used as intended, has no material residual utility, and has a supported salvage, rejection or destruction position. Severe appearance damage, corrosion concern or a planned destruction is not enough by itself.

For machinery and component claims, compare repair, cleaning, testing, replacement-part and complete-replacement options on a like-for-like basis, including technical feasibility, OEM or competent expert requirements, labour, freight, installation, commissioning, hygiene or safety standards, downtime only if insured, useful life, betterment, warranty and residual value.

Read the current policy and endorsements in full. Apply only the evidenced Institute Cargo Clauses, warehouse-to-warehouse or port-to-port duration, customs-storage period, clean-transport-document and preliminary-survey warranties, packing and under-deck conditions, container and replacement clauses, classification requirements, shortage certificates, deductibles, valuation, limits, and rust, oxidation, moisture, scratching, denting, delay or other exclusions.

Map each material term to established facts without inventing compliance, breach, cover or legal effect. All-risks wording does not remove the need to establish physical loss or damage during the insured transit and to test exclusions, warranties, duration and causation.

Keep original commercial invoice, replacement or pro-forma quotation, freight invoice, transport invoice, insured value, policy limit, presented claim, itemized affected value, repair estimate, labour, forwarding, refitting, packing surcharge, destruction cost, salvage and recovery separate. A quotation is not automatically an incurred cost or the policy measure of indemnity.

Calculate quantum locally line by line from supported quantity and rate. Verify extensions, dimensions or weights, allocate freight or charges only on a supported basis, apply the evidenced exchange rate and date, then the policy uplift, deductible, salvage, depreciation and recovery in the correct order. Preserve source arithmetic conflicts instead of forcing the historical total.

Admit survey, segregation, mitigation, forwarding, repair, destruction or other expenses only when they are evidenced, reasonable, causally related and recoverable under the current policy. Reject unlawful payments, unsupported penalties, internal estimates and unrelated business costs from the insured adjustment.

Do not apply a hypothetical or percentage recovery deduction merely because notice was late. Quantify recovery or prejudice only from supported liability, limitation, weight, declared value, contract, jurisdiction, evidence preservation and realistic recovery prospects, subject to professional and legal review.

Recovery analysis must distinguish carrier, actual carrier, agent, terminal, stevedore, inland haulier, shipper, packer, supplier, warehouse and other candidates. Test the front and reverse transport terms, custody, clean or claused receipt, reservations, notice, joint-survey invitation, causation, unseaworthy or unsuitable equipment evidence, limitation, jurisdiction, time bar, security and recovery economics before recommending pursuit.

Select the strongest supported outcome branch: no established loss, partial breakage or damage, repairable machinery or component loss, evidenced total loss, seawater or freshwater wetting, rust or contamination, shortage or non-delivery, packing or handling-related loss, an excluded or warranty-affected claim, or a covered loss below the deductible.

Use representative current-claim photographs of loading, packing, stowage, lashing, container exterior and interior, roof or door defects, seals, delivery condition, affected and sound comparison items, testing, segregation, repair, salvage and destruction under the global Appendix limits.

The global ULA report specification, Director wording, no-fabrication rules, deterministic calculations, citation requirements, empty Enclosure and Outstanding sections, Appendix limits, and human approval gates override every unsupported cause or liability statement, unreconciled quantity, screening-test overstatement, arbitrary recovery percentage, line-item arithmetic error, conclusion order, or legacy appendix practice in a historical Non-Reefer report.
